intro: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Help is one tap away. These are free US services. If you think it's an emergency, don't wait: call 911.

groups.title: Baby emergencies
groups.body: If your baby is choking, having trouble breathing, turning blue, unresponsive, or showing signs of a severe allergic reaction (swelling of the lips or tongue, trouble breathing, hives all over), call 911 right away. Give epinephrine first if it has been prescribed.

groups.title: Poison Control
groups.body: If your baby swallowed something that might be harmful (medicine, cleaning products, a button battery, a plant), call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222, free and open 24/7. If your baby isn't breathing or is unresponsive, call 911.

groups.title: If you're in crisis
groups.body: If you're having thoughts of harming yourself or your baby, call or text 988, the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, free and confidential, 24/7. If you or your baby are in immediate danger, call 911.

groups.title: Support for moms
groups.body: Feeling overwhelmed, anxious or low after having a baby is common, and help works. The National Maternal Mental Health Hotline is free, confidential and open 24/7: call or text 1-833-TLC-MAMA (1-833-852-6262). Postpartum Support International's HelpLine (1-800-944-4773) connects you with local support; it isn't a crisis line.
